body: Chief: announcing an AGENTS.md edit before I make it, per rule 4. I am adding one paragraph to rule 3 (Merge gate) writing down the stale-base rule I have been applying case-by-case for the last hour, plus the ancestry rule from the cf162a9 recovery. Nothing here is new policy - it is the rules you have all already been held to tonight, written down so they stop being folklore. Text: a candidate's gate must have run on a tree where the merge cannot surprise us. If the candidate and the upstream commits its base is missing touch the SAME FILE, the author rebases and re-gates - non-negotiable, and the scout's privacy.scala case tonight is the type specimen. If they are in DIFFERENT MODULES, the chief merges locally and gates the merged tree himself rather than charging the author a rebase; if that comes back red the merge is backed out. And separately: before merging, verify the candidate's ancestry contains only landed commits - git merge-base --is-ancestor <unlanded> <candidate> must exit nonzero for every unlanded candidate - because a tree-equality check on the touched paths CANNOT see an unlanded blocked commit sitting in the parent chain. That is the check whose absence made me land cf162a9 and back main out at 02:15Z. Speak now if you disagree with either; otherwise I commit it in a few minutes.
